answers.solution:
Solution written to **`/workspace/solution.md`** (copy at **`~/solution.md`**).

## What I did

The environment had no repo — only `/workspace/problem.json`. I built a faithful minimal reproduction of the gate (`/tmp/repro_full.sh`), confirmed both failure modes, applied the fix, and verified both directions plus the ancillary trap.

## Root cause

The arm is a **whole-index grep**, not a diff grep:

- The index is a full tree snapshot seeded from HEAD, so `git grep --cached` sees committed offenders even when the current commit doesn't touch them.
- The arm switches to index mode if **anything** is staged (even one board row), so every commit fails while the offenders sit in the index.
- Editing the offenders in the worktree doesn't touch the index, so the arm keeps reading HEAD's committed copy.

## Fix (the key move is staging)

```bash
PATTERN='/home/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/'
sed -i -E 's#/home/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+#~#g' reports/run-a.json reports/run-b.log
git diff -- reports/run-a.json reports/run-b.log   # only path prefix changed
git add reports/run-a.json reports/run-b.log       # <-- makes the arm grade the fixed index
git commit -m "sanitize(reports): absolute host-home path -> ~"
# => ARM home-path: PASS baseline 0 / current 0 (scope index) / SELFTEST: PASS / EXIT=0
```

## Verification results (from the run)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Board-only commit | `FAIL baseline 0 / current 2 (scope index)`, EXIT=1 |
| Repair edited, not staged | `FAIL baseline 0 / current 2 (scope index)`, EXIT=1 |
| Repair staged, commit through hook | `PASS baseline 0 / current 0 (scope index)`, EXIT=0 |
| Committed-tree offender count | `0` |
| Index offender count | `0` |
| Fix commit tree matches hook's `tree=… rc=0` log line | yes |
| Payload/provenance bytes | identical; only `~` → `~` |
| Scratch worktree grading of HEAD (residual) | `PASS baseline 0 / current 0 (scope HEAD)` |
| `--no-verify` contrast | offender count `1`, zero gated attempts logged → bypass detectable |

Also documented: don't raise `guards/home-path.baseline` to 2; the concurrent-harvester trap (verify landed content via `git show HEAD:<path>` and use a forward corrective commit, never rewrite shared history); and the `git grep` option-order trap I actually hit (`--cached` after a positional pattern is parsed as a revision — keep it before the pattern or use `-e`).

signatures.description: A pre-commit publication gate (a grep arm inside a repo's own selftest, wired as guards.test_command) greps the INDEX when anything is staged and HEAD otherwise, excluding a few paths. Two artifacts committed after the gate was last closed at baseline 0 reintroduced forbidden absolute host-home paths (/home/<user>/...). Because the arm grades the index, every commit that does not itself stage the repair sees the offenders and fails: a board-only commit from a sibling lane fails on a row unrelated to its own diff, and the lane that would fix it sees HEAD's copy while its edit sits in the working tree. Diagnosed by reading the guard log's arm line (baseline 0, current 2 + the two paths) and grepping HEAD with the same regex to confirm the offenders are committed, not merely dirty. Resolution: sanitize the two artifacts in the working tree (absolute host-home path -> ~ form, measured outputs and provenance tokens byte-identical), STAGE the repair, then commit through the hook so the arm grades the fixed index - it prints PASS baseline 0 / current 0 and the suite ends SELFTEST: PASS / EXIT=0. Do not reach for --no-verify: it hides the one arm you are repairing. Verification that both directions hold: count offenders in the committed tree (must be 0) and confirm the fix commit was created through the hook (guard log has the PASS arm line, not a bypass). Residual worth naming in the closure: the arm cannot be proven from a clean HEAD alone, only from a staged index or a scratch checkout of HEAD; if that matters, add a second grading of a scratch checkout. Ancillary trap hit in the same tick: a concurrent harvester lane committed the staged board rows under its own message, so verify the LANDED tree's row content and add a tree-true corrective commit instead of rewriting shared history.
